option_description: Controls the enforcement action taken by the inbound mail gateway when SPF checks fail for a received message. Options range from outright rejection to silent pass-through, determining whether unauthorized senders are blocked, held for review, tagged, or allowed unconditionally.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires spf_policy_enforcement to be 'reject' or 'quarantine' for the sender_authentication_enforcement countermeasure to activate. A value of 'tag_only' or 'none' means spoofed messages reach recipients, bypassing the cryptographic sender verification layer entirely. Combined with dkim_validation_enabled and dmarc_policy_enforcement, this setting forms the first layer of the three-protocol authentication chain that prevents domain spoofing and phishing delivery.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Postfix/SpamAssassin or Milter policy daemon logs to identify current SPF failure handling directives.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i 'spf' /etc/postfix/main.cf | grep -E 'reject|quarantine|discard|pass'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A line such as 'smtpd_recipient_restrictions = ... reject_invalid_helo_hostname, check_policy_service ...' or a policyd-spf stanza indicating the fail action.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the python-policyd-spf or pypolicyd-spf configuration file for the Mail_Fail_Action directive, which maps directly to SPF hard-fail enforcement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A line such as 'Mail_Fail_Action = Reject' or 'Mail_Fail_Action = Quarantine' or '550 5.7.1 SPF check failed'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender portal, navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam policies and review the SPF hard fail action under each inbound policy.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender Portal > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam > Inbound policy > Edit spam threshold and properties > Mark as spam: SPF record: hard fail
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Setting shows 'On' with an associated action of 'Move message to Junk Email folder', 'Quarantine', or 'Reject'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the Microsoft Graph / Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve anti-spam policy SPF enforcement settings.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, SpamAction, MarkAsSpamSpfRecordHardFail | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output listing MarkAsSpamSpfRecordHardFail as 'On' or 'Off' and SpamAction indicating the enforcement disposition.

option_description: Controls whether the inbound mail server or gateway actively verifies DKIM cryptographic signatures on received messages. When enabled, the mail system checks that the signing domain's public key matches the signature embedded in the message header, confirming message integrity and sender authorization.
security_impact: The Rego sender_authentication_enforcement rule requires dkim_validation_enabled == true in every evaluation branch, making it a mandatory condition with no fallback. If DKIM validation is disabled, the policy cannot activate regardless of SPF or DMARC settings, leaving the authentication chain incomplete. DKIM validation detects message tampering in transit and is the mechanism through which DMARC alignment on the DKIM path is achieved, which is particularly important when SPF checks fail due to forwarding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether a DKIM verification milter (e.g., OpenDKIM or Rspamd) is loaded and active in Postfix.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n smtpd_milters non_smtpd_milters | grep -i dkim; systemctl is-active opendkim rspamd 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: smtpd_milters contains a socket reference to opendkim or rspamd, and systemctl reports 'active' for the relevant service.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the OpenDKIM configuration to confirm it is operating in verification mode for inbound mail.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode contains 'v' (verify) — e.g., 'Mode    sv' or 'Mode    v' — confirming inbound signature verification is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Google Workspace Admin Console, verify DKIM authentication status for inbound mail processing.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Google Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Authenticate email > DKIM authentication section — review that inbound DKIM verification is shown as enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Status shows DKIM authentication is active and processing inbound messages.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to confirm DKIM inbound validation state across accepted domains.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-DkimSigningConfig | Select-Object Domain, Enabled, Status | Format-Table; Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableDkimCheck
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled column shows True and Status shows Valid for relevant domains; EnableDkimCheck shows True in filter policies.

option_description: Controls the enforcement action applied by the inbound mail gateway to messages that fail DMARC alignment checks — meaning neither SPF nor DKIM aligns with the RFC5322 From domain. The setting determines whether failing messages are rejected at the SMTP level, quarantined for review, monitored without action, or ignored entirely.
security_impact: Both Rego branches of sender_authentication_enforcement require dmarc_policy_enforcement to be 'reject' or 'quarantine'. A value of 'monitor_only' or 'none' means the gateway collects DMARC data but takes no protective action, allowing spoofed messages through to inboxes. DMARC enforcement is the policy layer that closes the gap left by SPF forwarding failures and unsigned messages, acting as the authoritative disposition instruction that overrides per-protocol verdicts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Rspamd or Amavis configuration for DMARC reject or quarantine action directives.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rn 'dmarc' /etc/rspamd/local.d/ /etc/rspamd/override.d/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'reject|quarantine|none|action'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines such as 'quarantine_enable = true;' or 'actions = { ... reject = ...; }' indicating DMARC enforcement disposition.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the OpenDMARC configuration file for the enforcement action applied on DMARC failure.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Directives such as 'RejectFailures true' for reject enforcement, or the absence of this setting indicating monitor-only mode.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, review the DMARC action settings within the anti-phishing policy and the default anti-spam policy's DMARC override settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-phishing > Edit policy > Unauthenticated sender section; also Anti-spam > Inbound policy > DMARC action fields.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DMARC policy section shows quarantine or reject action rather than 'Honor the DMARC policy p=none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Exchange Online PowerShell for DMARC-related configuration in anti-phishing and spoof intelligence policies.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, DmarcQuarantineAction, DmarcRejectAction, EnableSpoofIntelligence | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DmarcRejectAction or DmarcQuarantineAction set to an enforcing action such as 'Quarantine' or 'Reject' rather than 'None'.

option_description: Controls whether the spam filtering engine is active and processing inbound email messages. This is the master on/off switch for the probabilistic content scoring and classification system that evaluates messages against spam indicators before delivery.
security_impact: The Rego spam_filtering_accuracy rule requires spam_filter_enabled == true as a non-negotiable prerequisite in both evaluation branches. If this setting is false, no spam scoring, threshold comparison, or detection action occurs regardless of how spam_score_threshold or spam_action_on_detection are configured. The spam_filtering_accuracy countermeasure, which provides D3-CF Content Filtering and D3-MA Message Analysis defenses, cannot activate without this flag enabled. The default value is explicitly false, meaning deployments that have not consciously enabled spam filtering will have no protection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify that SpamAssassin, Rspamd, or the equivalent spam filtering service is running and integrated with the mail transport agent.
how_to_obtain.command: systemctl is-active spamassassin rspamd amavis 2>/dev/null; postconf -n content_filter smtpd_milters | grep -i spam
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one spam filtering service reports 'active' and Postfix content_filter or smtpd_milters references the spam scanning daemon.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Amavis or SpamAssassin configuration to confirm spam checking is not bypassed globally.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: File contains '@bypass_spam_checks_maps = (0);' or the spam check bypass is commented out, confirming spam scanning is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, confirm that at least one anti-spam inbound policy is in an enabled state and applies to the relevant recipients.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam > Inbound policies — verify the Default policy or custom policies show Status as 'On'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one inbound anti-spam policy shows Status 'On' with a priority and applicable recipients defined.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to list all hosted content filter policies and confirm at least one is enabled.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, IsDefault, SpamAction, HighConfidenceSpamAction | Format-Table; Get-HostedContentFilterRule | Select-Object Name, State, Priority | Format-Table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one policy rule shows State as 'Enabled' with an associated filter policy that has non-null SpamAction values.

option_description: Sets the numeric score value at or above which the spam filter classifies a message as spam and applies the configured enforcement action. The spam engine assigns cumulative point values based on content characteristics, header analysis, and reputation checks; this threshold determines the sensitivity of the classification boundary.
security_impact: The primary Rego branch for spam_filtering_accuracy checks spam_score_threshold <= 7, meaning only values of 7 or below (stricter filtering) satisfy the condition for the countermeasure to activate via that path. Values above 10 effectively disable filtering as very few messages accumulate scores that high, and values near the maximum of 100 provide no protection. An alternative Rego branch can satisfy the rule through header_analysis_checks depth, but a well-tuned threshold remains the primary control lever for false-positive/false-negative balance. Industry guidance places effective thresholds between 3 and 7.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SpamAssassin local configuration file for the required_score directive, which sets the classification threshold.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A line such as 'required_score 5.0' or 'required_score 7' indicating the current threshold value.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the active SpamAssassin configuration including site-wide and user-level overrides to find the effective required_score.
how_to_obtain.command: spamassassin --lint -D 2>&1 | grep -i required_score; grep -r 'required_score' /etc/spamassassin/ /etc/mail/spamassassin/ ~/.spamassassin/ 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing the numeric required_score value currently in effect, e.g., 'required_score: 5' or from the lint debug output.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Rspamd deployments, check the actions configuration which maps score thresholds to spam dispositions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Stanza showing numeric thresholds per action, e.g., 'reject = 15; add_header = 6; greylist = 4;' — the add_header value corresponds to the spam classification threshold.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender anti-spam policy, review the Spam threshold slider or the Bulk complaint level (BCL) and Spam confidence level (SCL) thresholds.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam > Edit inbound policy > Spam threshold and properties > Bulk email threshold (1-9 scale, lower = stricter).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bulk email threshold value between 1 and 9 visible; values of 4-7 are typical for organizations wanting balanced filtering.

option_description: Controls the enforcement action applied to messages that exceed the spam score threshold. This determines the final disposition of classified spam — whether it is rejected at the SMTP layer, held in quarantine for review, delivered with a spam tag in the subject or headers, or passed through without modification.
security_impact: Both Rego branches for spam_filtering_accuracy require spam_action_on_detection to be in ['reject', 'quarantine']. A value of 'tag' only modifies the message but delivers it to the inbox, relying on the end user to recognize it as spam. A value of 'none' means spam passes through even after being scored above the threshold. The default value is explicitly 'none', meaning out-of-the-box deployments that have not configured this action provide no actual filtering despite having the spam engine active. The countermeasure providing D3-CF Content Filtering and D3-MA Message Analysis cannot activate without an actionable disposition.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Amavis configuration for the spam_tag2_level and spam_kill_level directives along with the final_spam_destiny setting, which together determine the enforcement action.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines such as '$final_spam_destiny = D_REJECT;' or '$final_spam_destiny = D_BOUNCE;' or '$sa_kill_level_deflt = 6.31;' showing the spam disposition action.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Rspamd configuration for the action assigned at the spam threshold level.
how_to_obtain.command: rspamadm configdump actions 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'add_header|reject|quarantine|greylist'; grep -r 'action\|reject\|quarantine' /etc/rspamd/local.d/actions.conf 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing the action type assigned at the spam score boundary, e.g., 'add_header = 6;' meaning tag, or 'reject = 6;' meaning reject.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve the SpamAction and HighConfidenceSpamAction configured in each hosted content filter policy.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, SpamAction, HighConfidenceSpamAction, SpamQuarantineTag, BulkSpamAction | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SpamAction shows 'Quarantine', 'Reject', 'MoveToJmf' (tag/move), or 'AddXHeader' — confirming whether the action is enforcing or merely informational.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Google Workspace Gmail spam settings, review what happens to messages identified as spam by checking the spam filter action in the compliance and routing rules.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Google Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Spam, Phishing and Malware > Spam section — review whether spam is quarantined, rejected, or delivered with modification.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Spam handling section shows an active policy with 'Quarantine' or 'Reject' as the disposition rather than 'Deliver to spam folder only'.

option_description: Specifies the list of header-based analysis techniques that are active in the spam filter. These modules inspect structural and content properties of email headers — such as the chain of Received hops, the originating IP address, MIME structure consistency, and Content-Type field mismatches — to identify suspicious or malformed messages characteristic of spam or spoofing.
security_impact: The second Rego branch for spam_filtering_accuracy checks count(input.header_analysis_checks) >= 3, meaning if at least three header analysis checks are active, the spam filtering countermeasure can activate even if spam_score_threshold exceeds 7. This provides an alternative path to the countermeasure for environments that rely on header intelligence rather than score-based thresholds. An empty array (the default) disables this path entirely. Active header analysis checks contribute to D3-CF Content Filtering, D3-SRA Sender Reputation Analysis, and D3-MA Message Analysis defensive techniques. The more checks enabled, the higher the detection fidelity for header-manipulation-based spam and phishing techniques.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect SpamAssassin plugin configuration directory to identify which header analysis plugins are loaded and enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Uncommented 'loadplugin' lines for relevant plugins such as 'Mail::SpamAssassin::Plugin::HeaderEval', 'RelayCountry', 'URIDNSBL', indicating active header analysis modules.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List active Rspamd modules to identify which header inspection modules are loaded, particularly those performing received chain, IP, and MIME analysis.
how_to_obtain.command: rspamadm configdump -m 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'mime|received|ip|header|content_type'; grep -rn 'enabled\s*=\s*true' /etc/rspamd/local.d/ | grep -Ei 'mime|spf|dkim|received|header'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output listing enabled modules such as 'mime_types', 'received_headers', 'ip_score', confirming header analysis checks that are active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review SpamAssassin rules files and check which header-based test categories are enabled, specifically looking for received chain, X-Originating-IP, MIME structure, and Content-Type tests.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -l 'X_ORIGINATING_IP\|RCVD_IN\|MIME_\|CONTENT_TYPE' /usr/share/spamassassin/*.cf 2>/dev/null | head -10; spamassassin -D --lint 2>&1 | grep -i 'plugin\|loaded' | grep -Ei 'mime|header|received'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rule files containing header analysis tests are listed, and plugin load messages confirm the relevant evaluation modules are active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Proofpoint, Mimecast, or similar email security gateway, navigate to the email filtering policy and review which header inspection rules are enabled under advanced anti-spam or header analysis settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Mimecast Administration Console > Administration > Gateway > Policies > Anti-Spam > Advanced Settings > Header Analysis Checks — review enabled/disabled state of individual header inspection modules.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of header analysis check modules with their enabled status; confirmed active checks should include at minimum received chain analysis, originating IP inspection, MIME structure validation, and Content-Type mismatch detection.

option_description: Controls whether a valid DMARC TXT record exists at the _dmarc.<domain> DNS location. This record is the foundation of DMARC enforcement, instructing receiving mail servers on how to handle unauthenticated messages purportedly from your domain.
security_impact: This is a prerequisite gate in the Rego policy: all three `dmarc_policy_disposition_automation` rules require `input.dmarc_record_present == true`. Without this record, DMARC quarantine and reject dispositions cannot be automated, leaving the domain fully exposed to spoofing. It is marked high criticality, and its absence means zero DMARC protection regardless of other configurations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the DNS TXT record for the DMARC location using dig. A valid response must return a record starting with 'v=DMARC1'.
how_to_obtain.command: dig TXT _dmarc.<your-domain>.com +short
how_to_obtain.expected_output: "v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com; pct=100"

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use nslookup as an alternative on Windows or cross-platform environments to verify the DMARC TXT record exists.
how_to_obtain.command: nslookup -type=TXT _dmarc.<your-domain>.com
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response contains a TXT record with 'v=DMARC1' as the first token.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the MXToolbox DMARC lookup tool to visually confirm the record exists and is syntactically valid, including parsing of all tags.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Navigate to https://mxtoolbox.com/DMARC.aspx, enter your domain name, and click 'DMARC Lookup'. Confirm the result shows a valid DMARC record with no syntax errors.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Green status indicator with record contents displayed; no 'Record Not Found' error.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Google Admin Toolbox DNS checker API to validate DMARC record presence programmatically across multiple domains.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s 'https://dns.google/resolve?name=_dmarc.<your-domain>.com&type=TXT' | python3 -m json.tool
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response with 'Answer' array containing a TXT record where 'data' field starts with 'v=DMARC1'.

option_description: Controls the enforcement action (p= tag) declared in the DMARC DNS record that receiving mail servers apply to messages failing DMARC evaluation. Values of 'none' provide monitoring only, 'quarantine' routes failing messages to spam/junk, and 'reject' causes outright delivery refusal.
security_impact: The Rego policy enforces this attribute in two rules: `dmarc_policy_disposition_automation` only activates when `dmarc_policy_level` is 'quarantine' or 'reject' (combined with pct=100), and `outbound_policy_enforcement` also references this field requiring 'reject' or 'quarantine' to satisfy the outbound signing rule. A value of 'none' leaves the domain in monitoring-only mode — unauthenticated spoofed messages are delivered without restriction, satisfying neither countermeasure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Extract the p= tag value directly from the DMARC DNS record using dig and grep.
how_to_obtain.command: dig TXT _dmarc.<your-domain>.com +short | grep -oP 'p=\K[^;]+'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One of: none, quarantine, or reject

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use a one-liner PowerShell command to resolve the DMARC record and parse the policy tag on Windows systems.
how_to_obtain.command: Resolve-DnsName -Name '_dmarc.<your-domain>.com' -Type TXT | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Strings | Where-Object { $_ -match 'v=DMARC1' } | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split ';') | Where-Object { $_ -match 'p=' } }
how_to_obtain.expected_output: String such as ' p=reject' or ' p=quarantine'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the DMARC Analyzer free lookup tool which parses and explicitly labels the policy disposition level.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Navigate to https://www.dmarcanalyzer.com/dmarc/dmarc-record-check/, enter your domain, and review the 'Policy' field in the results table.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy field displays 'reject', 'quarantine', or 'none' with a recommendation indicator.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review DMARC aggregate reports (rua= destination) to confirm how receiving servers are interpreting and applying the current policy declaration.
how_to_obtain.command: find /var/mail/dmarc-reports/ -name '*.xml' -newer /tmp/last_check | xargs -I{} xmllint --xpath '//policy_published/p/text()' {}
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All report files should show matching policy values consistent with the DNS record declaration.

option_description: Controls the pct= tag in the DMARC record, which specifies what percentage of messages failing DMARC alignment actually receive the enforcement action defined by the p= policy. A value of 100 means full enforcement; lower values allow gradual rollout by randomly sampling a portion of failing mail.
security_impact: The Rego `dmarc_policy_disposition_automation` rules require both `dmarc_policy_level` in quarantine/reject AND `dmarc_pct_value == 100` to activate. Any value below 100 means a portion of spoofed or unauthenticated messages bypass enforcement and reach recipients. For example, pct=50 with p=reject still delivers 50% of DMARC-failing mail. This is high criticality because partial enforcement provides false assurance while leaving meaningful attack surface.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Parse the pct= tag directly from the DMARC TXT record. If absent from the output, the effective value is 100 per RFC 7489.
how_to_obtain.command: dig TXT _dmarc.<your-domain>.com +short | grep -oP 'pct=\K[0-9]+'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integer between 0 and 100. No output means pct is implicitly 100.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use a Python one-liner to fetch and parse the pct tag, defaulting to 100 if absent, for scripted compliance checks.
how_to_obtain.command: python3 -c "import dns.resolver; recs = dns.resolver.resolve('_dmarc.<your-domain>.com', 'TXT'); raw = ''.join([s.decode() for r in recs for s in r.strings]); tags = dict(t.strip().split('=',1) for t in raw.split(';') if '=' in t); print('pct:', tags.get('pct', '100 (default)'))"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: pct: 100

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use MXToolbox DMARC lookup which explicitly calls out the pct value and flags values below 100 as partial enforcement.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Navigate to https://mxtoolbox.com/DMARC.aspx, run a lookup for your domain, and locate the 'Percentage' row in the parsed record table.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Percentage field shows '100' for full enforcement or a lower number indicating staged rollout.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the email administrator or review change management records to determine if the pct value was intentionally set below 100 for a phased deployment and whether a target completion date for full enforcement exists.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation confirming pct=100 is the intended final state, with a timeline if currently below 100.

option_description: Controls whether deep email header chain inspection is actively enabled on the mail server or security gateway. This encompasses parsing and analysis of all RFC 5322 header fields including Received chains, From, Reply-To, Return-Path, and X-Originating-IP for anomaly detection.
security_impact: This is a mandatory prerequisite in both `header_inspection_depth` Rego rules — both conditions begin with `input.header_inspection_enabled == true`. Without this enabled, display name spoofing checks, reply-to mismatch actions, and hop count monitoring cannot activate regardless of how those individual controls are configured. It is rated high criticality and serves as the gateway control for all header-based phishing and routing anomaly detection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft 365 Defender: check the anti-phishing policy settings to confirm header inspection and advanced phishing thresholds are enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender Portal > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-phishing > Select active policy > Review 'Phishing threshold & protection' section for 'Advanced phishing thresholds' set to 2 or higher.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Advanced phishing threshold enabled at level 2 (Aggressive) or higher, confirming header inspection is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Exchange Online PowerShell to confirm anti-phishing policy header inspection settings are active.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled, PhishThresholdLevel, EnableMailboxIntelligence | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled: True, PhishThresholdLevel: 2 or higher

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix with a header inspection milter (e.g., rspamd or SpamAssassin), check the milter configuration to confirm header analysis rules are loaded and active.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n | grep -E 'milter|header_checks'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: header_checks = regexp:/etc/postfix/header_checks and smtpd_milters entries pointing to active filter socket

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review mail gateway logs for evidence that header inspection rules are firing — look for header-based filter hits in recent message processing records.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i 'header' /var/log/maillog | grep -iE 'inspection|check|rule|matched' | tail -50
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries showing header rule evaluations applied to inbound messages, confirming the feature is active.

option_description: Controls whether the mail filtering system actively inspects inbound messages for mismatches between the sender's display name and the actual email address domain. For example, detecting a message where the display name is 'CEO John Smith' but the From address is attacker@evil.com.
security_impact: Referenced in both `header_inspection_depth` Rego rules — both conditions require `input.display_name_spoofing_check == true` alongside `header_inspection_enabled`. This control directly counters Business Email Compromise (BEC) and executive impersonation attacks where adversaries spoof trusted identities without needing to compromise the actual domain. High criticality because display name spoofing bypasses SPF/DKIM/DMARC entirely since the attacker uses their own legitimate domain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft 365 Defender, verify impersonation protection rules checking display name against known internal users are configured in the anti-phishing policy.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender Portal > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-phishing > Edit active policy > Impersonation section > Confirm 'Enable users to protect' list includes executive/sensitive accounts and 'If message is detected as user impersonation' action is set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Protected users list populated with key internal accounts; action set to quarantine or move to junk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Exchange Online PowerShell for impersonation protection settings that implement display name spoofing detection.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableTargetedUserProtection, TargetedUsersToProtect, TargetedUserProtectionAction | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EnableTargetedUserProtection: True, TargetedUsersToProtect populated, TargetedUserProtectionAction: Quarantine or MoveToJmf

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Proofpoint Email Protection, query the management API to confirm spoofing rules targeting display name mismatches are active.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u '<admin>:<apikey>' 'https://<proofpoint-host>/api/v1/filter/policies' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -A5 'display_name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy entry with display_name spoofing rule showing 'enabled': true

how_to_obtain.instruction: For rspamd, check the DMARC and phishing module configuration for display name check rules targeting known internal identities.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'display_name\|from_name' /etc/rspamd/ --include='*.conf' --include='*.lua'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries enabling from_name mismatch checks with associated scoring or reject actions.

option_description: Controls the enforcement action taken when the Reply-To header domain differs from the From header domain in an inbound message. This mismatch is a common indicator of reply-hijacking attacks where attackers craft messages that appear to come from a trusted source but redirect replies to an attacker-controlled address.
security_impact: Referenced in the first `header_inspection_depth` Rego rule which requires `input.reply_to_mismatch_action in ["tag", "quarantine", "reject"]`. A value of 'none' means the system detects the mismatch but takes no action, leaving users vulnerable to reply redirection attacks that harvest sensitive information. Medium criticality reflects that this is a social engineering vector rather than direct delivery of malware, but it is highly effective in BEC scenarios.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft 365, check transport rules (mail flow rules) for a rule that inspects Reply-To vs From domain mismatch and applies a corresponding action.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Admin Center > Exchange Admin Center > Mail Flow > Rules > Review rules for conditions matching 'Header matches' with Reply-To domain patterns and actions of 'Apply disclaimer', 'Redirect', or 'Reject'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active transport rule with Reply-To domain mismatch condition and a non-'none' enforcement action applied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Exchange Online PowerShell to list all transport rules and identify any that handle Reply-To versus From domain mismatches.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-TransportRule | Where-Object {$_.Conditions -match 'ReplyTo' -or $_.Description -match 'reply-to'} | Select-Object Name, State, Actions | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more transport rules in 'Enabled' state with quarantine, reject, or tag/disclaimer actions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For SpamAssassin, check custom rule files for Reply-To domain mismatch scoring rules that would flag or reject such messages.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'REPLYTO\|reply_to\|Reply-To' /etc/spamassassin/ /etc/mail/spamassassin/ --include='*.cf'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rule entries such as 'header REPLYTO_DOMAIN_MISMATCH' with associated score and describe entries.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix with milter integration, check header_checks configuration for Reply-To domain inspection rules.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i 'reply-to\|reply_to' /etc/postfix/header_checks /etc/postfix/mime_header_checks 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Regex entries matching Reply-To domain patterns with REJECT, HOLD, or WARN actions.

option_description: Controls whether a maximum hop-count threshold is configured on Received headers in inbound messages. Each mail relay adds a Received header; an unusually high number of hops can indicate message laundering, routing obfuscation, or evasion of sender reputation checks. This boolean is true when a threshold greater than zero is actively configured.
security_impact: Referenced in the second `header_inspection_depth` Rego rule which evaluates `input.max_received_hops_exceeded > 0` alongside header inspection and display name spoofing checks. Anomalous hop counts are a forensic indicator used to detect messages deliberately routed through multiple intermediaries to obscure origin. Low criticality reflects it as a supplementary signal rather than a primary blocking control, but it contributes to the header inspection depth countermeasure score when active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix, check if a maximum_hop_count parameter is set, which controls rejection of messages with excessive Received headers.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n | grep 'hop_count\|max_hop'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: hopcount_limit = 50 (or similar configured value). Default is 50 if not explicitly set.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Postfix main.cf file for the hopcount_limit parameter which defines the maximum number of Received headers before rejection.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i 'hopcount\|hop_count\|max.*hop' /etc/postfix/main.cf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Entry such as 'hopcount_limit = 25' confirming a threshold is configured; absence means default of 50 applies.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft 365 Defender advanced hunting, query for messages with high Received header counts to confirm the platform is tracking and flagging anomalous routing depth.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender Portal > Hunting > Advanced Hunting > Run KQL query to inspect email metadata for Received header chain depth analysis in EmailEvents table.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Query results showing emails flagged or filtered based on anomalous hop counts in the NetworkMessageId records.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For SpamAssassin, check for RECEIVED_SPAM_RELAYS or custom hop-count rules that score or flag messages based on excessive Received headers.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'hop\|HOPS\|received.*count\|MAX_RECEIVED' /etc/spamassassin/ --include='*.cf' | grep -v '^#'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rule definitions with hop count thresholds such as 'header __MANY_RECEIVED Received =~ /./g' count checks with associated scoring.

option_description: Controls whether the email platform routes inbound URLs and file attachments to an integrated sandboxing engine for pre-delivery detonation and behavioral analysis before messages reach recipients.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires this to be true as the first condition for the url_and_attachment_sandboxing_integration countermeasure. Without it, no dynamic analysis occurs and all subsequent sandbox configuration attributes (verdict action, scope, inbound scope) are irrelevant. Disabling this leaves the organization with no pre-delivery malicious content detonation, exposing users to zero-day payloads in attachments and phishing URLs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Defender for Office 365, navigate to Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Attachments, then review each policy to confirm the policy is enabled and not in Monitor-only mode. For Google Workspace, navigate to Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Safety > Enhanced pre-delivery message scanning and confirm it is toggled on.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Security Center: Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Attachments | Google Admin Console: Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Safety
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy status shows 'On' with an action other than 'Monitor' or 'Off'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 REST API to retrieve Safe Attachments policy details and confirm the Enable property is set to true.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-ExchangeOnline; Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enable, Action | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enable : True for each policy in scope, with Action not set to 'Allow'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Proofpoint on-premises, query the management API or review the TAP (Targeted Attack Protection) configuration file to confirm sandboxing is active.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -i 'sandbox\|detonation\|tap_enabled' /etc/proofpoint/pps.conf 2>/dev/null || curl -s -u admin:password https://proofpoint-host/api/v2/threat/policies | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i sandbox
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entry shows sandboxing or TAP enabled = true/yes/1.

option_description: Defines the enforcement action applied when the sandboxing engine returns a malicious verdict for a URL or attachment — determining whether the message is blocked before delivery, quarantined, replaced with a safe version, merely monitored/logged, or allowed through.
security_impact: The Rego policy checks that sandbox_verdict_action is one of block, quarantine, or replace for the url_and_attachment_sandboxing_integration countermeasure to activate. A value of monitor or allow means malicious content is not stopped before delivery despite being detected — the sandbox provides intelligence but zero protection. This is a critical gap: sandboxing in audit-only mode provides visibility but no actual threat prevention.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Defender for Office 365, navigate to Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Attachments, open each policy, and inspect the 'Safe Attachments unknown malware response' setting. Valid enforcement values are 'Block', 'Replace', or 'Dynamic Delivery'. For Safe Links, confirm 'Real-time URL scanning' is enforced with block actions.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Security Center: Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Attachments > [Policy Name] > Action
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Action field shows 'Block', 'Replace', or 'Dynamic Delivery' — not 'Monitor' or 'Off'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve the Action property from all Safe Attachment policies and confirm enforcement-level values.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-ExchangeOnline; Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy | Select-Object Name, Action, Enable | Where-Object {$_.Enable -eq $true} | Format-Table -AutoSize
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Action column displays 'Block', 'Replace', or 'DynamicDelivery' for all enabled policies.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Mimecast, use the Mimecast API to retrieve the attachment protection policy and inspect the action field returned in the policy object.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://api.mimecast.com/api/policy/definitions/get-policy' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"data":[{"policyType":"attachment"}]}' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i 'action\|verdict'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response contains action field with value block, quarantine, or replace.

option_description: Specifies which content types are submitted to the sandboxing engine for dynamic analysis. Should include both 'urls' and 'attachments' to achieve complete pre-delivery coverage of threat vectors carried in email messages.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires both 'urls' in input.sandbox_scope and 'attachments' in input.sandbox_scope for the url_and_attachment_sandboxing_integration countermeasure to activate. Configuring only one content type creates a blind spot — organizations that sandbox attachments but not URLs remain vulnerable to phishing via embedded links, and vice versa. Complete scope coverage is mandatory for the countermeasure to be recognized as active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Defender for Office 365, review both Safe Attachments policies (for attachment scope) and Safe Links policies (for URL scope). Confirm Safe Links is configured to scan URLs in email messages and that Safe Attachments covers file types. In Google Workspace, check Admin Console > Gmail > Safety for both 'Enhanced pre-delivery message scanning' (attachments) and 'Protect against anomalous attachment types' as well as link scanning settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Safe Attachments: Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Attachments | Safe Links: Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Links
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Both attachment sandboxing policy and URL/link scanning policy are enabled and configured for inbound mail.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to check Safe Links policy settings for URL scanning scope alongside Safe Attachment policies.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-ExchangeOnline; Write-Host '--- Safe Links ---'; Get-SafeLinksPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableSafeLinksForEmail, ScanUrls, EnableForInternalSenders | Format-List; Write-Host '--- Safe Attachments ---'; Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enable, Action | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EnableSafeLinksForEmail and ScanUrls are True; Safe Attachments Enable is True — confirming both urls and attachments are in scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Proofpoint TAP, query the API to retrieve which content categories are submitted for sandboxing analysis.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u 'svc_account:password' 'https://tap-api-v2.proofpoint.com/v2/settings' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'url|attachment|sandbox|scope'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response includes both URL and attachment content types listed as active sandbox submission categories.

option_description: Determines whether the sandboxing policy is scoped to cover inbound email traffic originating from external senders. Without inbound scope, sandboxing may only apply to internal or outbound mail and leave externally delivered threats unanalyzed.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires policy_applies_to_inbound == true as a necessary condition for the url_and_attachment_sandboxing_integration countermeasure. External inbound email is the primary attack vector for malicious attachments and phishing URLs. A sandboxing policy scoped only to internal or outbound traffic provides no protection against the most common email threat delivery path, rendering the entire sandboxing investment ineffective for inbound threat prevention.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Defender for Office 365, open each Safe Attachments and Safe Links policy and review the 'Applied To' section. Confirm the policy condition includes 'The recipient domain is [your-domain.com]' or 'All recipients' with no exclusion that would exempt externally delivered messages. The policy must not be restricted to internal senders only.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Safe Attachments > [Policy] > Users, groups, and domains
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy is applied to all recipient domains or specific internal domains, covering messages delivered from external senders.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to inspect Safe Attachment rules and confirm the rule conditions include inbound mail flow without restrictions to internal senders only.

how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rules show recipient domain conditions covering internal domains with no exclusion that would bypass inbound external mail.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix/Amavis-based environments, inspect the Amavis configuration to confirm content_filter applies to inbound SMTP connections from external hosts.

how_to_obtain.expected_output: No bypass rules present for external sender domains; content_filter applies to all inbound connections.

option_description: Controls whether the email server or gateway produces structured, persistent logs for all inbound and outbound message events, capturing the full mail flow record required for forensic analysis and compliance auditing.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires logging_enabled == true as the foundational condition for the delivery_log_completeness countermeasure. Without logging enabled, none of the required fields (authentication_result, filter_verdict, delivery_status, timestamp) can be captured, and the retention requirement becomes moot. Disabled logging eliminates the organization's ability to perform post-incident forensic reconstruction of email-based attacks and undermines compliance with frameworks requiring audit trails (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA).

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Postfix servers, verify that the mail log is being written by checking syslog configuration and confirming the log file is actively receiving entries.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n | grep -E 'syslog|log_level|maillog'; ls -lh /var/log/mail.log /var/log/maillog 2>/dev/null; tail -5 /var/log/mail.log 2>/dev/null || tail -5 /var/log/maillog 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mail log file exists, has recent modification timestamp, and contains current SMTP session entries.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Exchange Admin Center, navigate to Mail Flow > Message Trace and run a recent trace. If results return successfully with delivery details, message logging is active. For Exchange on-premises, check the Exchange Admin Center under Servers > Servers > [Server] > Transport Logs to confirm logging paths are configured.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Exchange Admin Center: Mail Flow > Message Trace | On-premises: Servers > [Server] > Transport Logs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Message trace returns results with sender, recipient, timestamp, and status fields populated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Microsoft Exchange on-premises, verify transport logging is enabled via PowerShell for both Send and Receive connectors.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-TransportService | Select-Object Name, MessageTrackingLogEnabled, MessageTrackingLogPath, MessageTrackingLogMaxAge | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MessageTrackingLogEnabled returns True with a valid log path and non-zero retention age.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Exim mail servers, verify logging directives in the main configuration file to confirm log_file_path and log_selector are configured for comprehensive message logging.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E '^log_file_path|^log_selector|^MAIN_LOG' /etc/exim4/exim4.conf.template /etc/exim/exim.conf 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: log_file_path points to an active log directory; log_selector includes +smtp_connection, +all, or equivalent comprehensive flags.

option_description: Specifies the set of event field types captured per message event in the mail log. Complete coverage requires fields including authentication_result, filter_verdict, delivery_status, sender, recipient, and timestamp to support forensic reconstruction and compliance auditing.
security_impact: The Rego policy checks that authentication_result, filter_verdict, delivery_status, and timestamp are all present in logged_fields for the delivery_log_completeness countermeasure. Missing any of these fields degrades the forensic value of logs — without authentication_result you cannot determine if SPF/DKIM/DMARC passed; without filter_verdict you cannot reconstruct why a message was delivered or blocked; without delivery_status and timestamp you cannot establish timeline and outcome. Incomplete field coverage breaks incident response workflows.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample actual log entries from the mail server or SIEM to identify which fields are present. Parse a recent log file and enumerate the distinct field names or key-value pairs captured per message event.
how_to_obtain.command: tail -100 /var/log/mail.log | grep 'status=\|from=\|to=\|auth=\|verdict=' | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log lines contain fields for sender (from=), recipient (to=), timestamp, delivery status (status=sent/deferred/bounced), and authentication or filter results.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Microsoft Exchange on-premises, review message tracking log field coverage by examining a sample tracking log entry to confirm all required fields are recorded.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-MessageTrackingLog -Start (Get-Date).AddHours(-1) -ResultSize 5 | Select-Object Timestamp, Sender, Recipients, MessageSubject, Source, EventId, TotalBytes, Status | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output includes Timestamp, Sender, Recipients, Status, and EventId fields for each tracked message event.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, navigate to Security > Reporting > Email & Collaboration > Message Trace, run a trace, and expand a result record to view all available fields. Verify authentication_result (DKIM/SPF/DMARC outcome), filter_verdict (spam/malware verdict), delivery_status, and timestamp are visible in the detailed view.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender: Security > Reports > Email & collaboration > Message trace > Run trace > View details
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Detailed message trace record shows Authentication results (SPF, DKIM, DMARC pass/fail), Filter verdict, Delivery status, and Date/time fields.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Microsoft Graph API for mail message trace data to programmatically enumerate the fields returned and confirm required fields are captured.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' 'https://reports.office.com/ecp/reportingwebservice/reporting.svc/MessageTrace?$select=StartDate,EndDate,FromAddress,ToAddress,Status,Subject&$top=1&$format=json' | python3 -m json.tool
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response includes FromAddress, ToAddress, Status, StartDate fields — map to sender, recipient, delivery_status, timestamp.

option_description: Specifies the number of days that mail delivery logs are retained before deletion or archival. This controls the window of forensic evidence available for incident investigation and the organization's ability to satisfy compliance audit log retention requirements.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires log_retention_days >= 90 as a necessary condition for the delivery_log_completeness countermeasure. Retention below 90 days limits the organization's ability to investigate email-based incidents that are discovered weeks or months after occurrence — a common pattern for supply-chain and BEC attacks. Many compliance frameworks (PCI DSS requires 1 year, HIPAA recommends 6 years, SOC 2 typically requires 1 year) mandate retention periods well beyond 90 days. Insufficient retention means log data is deleted before it can be used in investigations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Microsoft Exchange on-premises, retrieve the message tracking log retention configuration to determine the MaxAge setting.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-TransportService | Select-Object Name, MessageTrackingLogMaxAge, MessageTrackingLogMaxDirectorySize, MessageTrackingLogPath | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MessageTrackingLogMaxAge shows a value of 90.00:00:00 or greater (format: days.hours:minutes:seconds).

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix with logrotate, inspect the logrotate configuration to determine the rotate count and frequency, then calculate total retention days (e.g., weekly with rotate 52 = 364 days).
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog /etc/logrotate.d/syslog 2>/dev/null; logrotate --debug /etc/logrotate.conf 2>&1 | grep -E 'mail|rotate|days'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: rotate N with weekly/daily frequency; calculated retention equals or exceeds 90 days.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For cloud email platforms forwarding to a SIEM (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Chronicle), check the SIEM data retention policy for the email log index or table. In Microsoft Sentinel, navigate to Settings > Workspace Settings > Usage and estimated costs > Data Retention and verify the retention period for the email-related tables.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft Sentinel: Settings > Workspace Settings > Usage and estimated costs > Data Retention | Splunk: Settings > Indexes > [email_index] > Retention
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retention period shows 90 days or greater for the mail log data source.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft 365, query the compliance center to retrieve audit log retention policies that cover email activity.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-IPPSSession; Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy | Select-Object Name, RetentionDuration, IsSimpleRetentionPolicy | Format-List; Get-ComplianceTag | Where-Object {$_.RetentionEnabled -eq $true} | Select-Object Name, RetentionDuration | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RetentionDuration shows a value equivalent to 90 days or greater for policies covering email content.

option_description: Controls whether the email server cryptographically signs all outbound messages with a DKIM private key before delivery, embedding a verifiable digital signature that receiving servers can validate against the public key published in DNS.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires dkim_signing_enabled == true as the mandatory first condition in both branches of the outbound_policy_enforcement countermeasure. Without DKIM signing, outbound messages carry no cryptographic proof of origin, making the organization's domain easier to spoof and damaging sender reputation when receiving servers cannot verify message authenticity. DKIM is also required for DMARC alignment — without DKIM signatures, DMARC can only align via SPF, which breaks in forwarding scenarios, causing legitimate mail to fail authentication at the recipient.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send a test email from the organization's mail system to a Gmail or Outlook.com account, then view the original message headers and look for a DKIM-Signature header. Alternatively, use a mail testing service to verify DKIM signing.
how_to_obtain.command: echo 'Subject: DKIM Test' | sendmail -v test@gmail.com 2>&1; # Then check received headers for DKIM-Signature field
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Received message headers contain a DKIM-Signature header with a valid d= (domain), s= (selector), and b= (signature) field.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Postfix with OpenDKIM, verify the milter integration is active and that a signing key is configured for the outbound domain.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n | grep -E 'milter|smtpd_milters|non_smtpd_milters'; systemctl status opendkim 2>/dev/null || service opendkim status 2>/dev/null; grep -E '^Domain|^KeyFile|^Selector|^SigningTable' /etc/opendkim.conf /etc/opendkim/opendkim.conf 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: smtpd_milters includes opendkim socket path; opendkim service is running; Domain, KeyFile, and Selector are configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft Exchange Online (Microsoft 365), retrieve the DKIM signing configuration for all accepted domains to confirm signing is enabled.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-ExchangeOnline; Get-DkimSigningConfig | Select-Object Domain, Enabled, Status, Selector1CNAME, Selector2CNAME | Format-Table -AutoSize
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled column shows True for all primary sending domains; Status shows Valid; CNAME records are populated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, navigate to Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Email Authentication Settings > DKIM and confirm that DKIM signing is enabled for each sending domain with a green checkmark and Status of 'Enabled'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender: Security > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Email Authentication Settings > DKIM
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each domain listed shows Enabled: Yes and Status: Normal/Valid with selector CNAME records confirmed in DNS.

option_description: Controls whether an SPF record or equivalent IP allowlist is published in DNS to restrict which IP ranges are authorized to send email on behalf of the organization's domain. Determines whether the policy is fully enforced (hard fail), permissive (soft fail), or absent entirely.
security_impact: Directly referenced in the outbound_policy_enforcement Rego rule, which requires authorized_sending_ip_policy == 'enforced' combined with dkim_signing_enabled and either a DMARC reject/quarantine policy or outbound spam filtering. Without enforcement, spoofed messages originating from unauthorized IPs can pass receiver-side SPF checks, undermining sender reputation and enabling phishing impersonation of the organization's domain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the domain's DNS TXT records for the SPF entry and evaluate the qualifier on the 'all' mechanism. A '-all' suffix indicates 'enforced', '~all' indicates 'permissive', and absence of any SPF record indicates 'none'.
how_to_obtain.command: dig +short TXT example.com | grep 'v=spf1'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: v=spf1 ip4:203.0.113.0/24 include:_spf.google.com -all (hard fail = enforced) or ~all (soft fail = permissive)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use nslookup to retrieve the SPF record on Windows environments or from a cross-platform shell, then inspect the all qualifier to classify policy state.
how_to_obtain.command: nslookup -type=TXT example.com | Select-String 'spf1'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Text = "v=spf1 ip4:... -all" where -all confirms enforced; ~all confirms permissive; no result confirms none

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender (security.microsoft.com), navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-phishing, then review the SPF record status under the domain's authentication settings. For Google Workspace, open Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Authenticate email to view SPF configuration.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365: security.microsoft.com > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-phishing | Google Workspace: admin.google.com > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Authenticate email
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SPF record listed with qualifier type displayed; domain authentication status shows pass/fail indicators

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the Microsoft Graph API to retrieve the domain's SPF verification status, or use a DNS-over-HTTPS API to programmatically retrieve and parse the TXT record for automation pipelines.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s 'https://dns.google/resolve?name=example.com&type=TXT' | python3 -c "import sys,json; [print(r['data']) for r in json.load(sys.stdin)['Answer'] if 'spf1' in r.get('data','')]"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response containing the SPF TXT record value; parse the all mechanism qualifier to determine policy state

option_description: Controls whether outbound email is routed through a content and spam scanning engine before leaving the organization's infrastructure. When enabled, messages are inspected for spam signatures, malicious content, and policy violations prior to external delivery.
security_impact: Referenced in the outbound_policy_enforcement Rego rule as an alternative qualifying condition: dkim_signing_enabled == true AND authorized_sending_ip_policy == 'enforced' AND outbound_spam_filtering_enabled == true. Without outbound filtering, compromised internal accounts or misconfigured applications can send spam or phishing campaigns externally, damaging sender reputation and potentially resulting in the organization's IP ranges being blocklisted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam. Locate the 'Anti-spam outbound policy (Default)' and verify it is enabled and assigned to all users or the appropriate policy scope.
how_to_obtain.navigation: security.microsoft.com > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam > Anti-spam outbound policy (Default)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy status shows 'On'; outbound rules are present and assigned to applicable users or groups

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve the outbound spam filter policy configuration and verify it is enabled with appropriate enforcement settings.
