how_to_obtain.instruction: For Google Workspace, navigate to Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Compliance and review outbound gateway or content compliance rules. Confirm a spam or content scanning rule is applied to outbound mail flows.
how_to_obtain.navigation: admin.google.com > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Compliance > Content compliance or Outbound gateway
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one active content compliance rule targeting outbound messages; outbound gateway configured to route through scanning appliance

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Exchange Online REST API or use PowerShell remoting to retrieve outbound filter rule assignments and confirm the policy is applied to all relevant senders.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterRule | Select-Object Name, State, Priority, SentToScope | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: State: Enabled; SentToScope covering all applicable outbound senders; Priority indicating rule ordering

option_description: Controls whether the email gateway or filtering platform supports hot-reload of filtering rules, blocklists, and authentication policies without requiring a service restart. When true, rule changes take effect immediately without causing mail flow interruption.
security_impact: Referenced in the rule_maintainability_and_updateability Rego rule, which requires live_rule_update_supported == true as a prerequisite for both automated/scheduled and manual update paths. Without live update support, deploying critical rule changes during active threat campaigns requires a service restart, creating either a protection gap or a mail flow outage, both of which increase organizational risk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review vendor documentation or release notes for the deployed email gateway product (e.g., Proofpoint, Mimecast, Cisco ESA, Postfix with milter plugins) to confirm whether rule hot-reload is a supported capability. Check for 'graceful reload', 'dynamic policy update', or 'live rule refresh' terminology.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Vendor documentation portal or admin console release notes
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation explicitly states rules can be updated without service restart; hot-reload or graceful reload feature listed as supported

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix-based deployments, test whether postmap and postfix reload apply new lookup tables without dropping connections. For Cisco ESA CLI, check whether commit activates rule changes without restart.
how_to_obtain.command: postfix reload && echo 'Reload successful without restart'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Command completes with 'postfix/postfix-script: refreshing the Postfix mail system' without service interruption indicator

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Proofpoint Email Protection, navigate to System > General Settings > Service Management and verify that rule updates are applied via dynamic refresh. In Mimecast Administration Console, check Gateway > Policies and confirm policy saves take effect immediately without gateway restart prompts.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Proofpoint: System > General Settings > Service Management | Mimecast: Administration Console > Gateway > Policies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No restart required message upon policy save; documentation or UI tooltip confirms live update behavior

how_to_obtain.instruction: For open-source or self-hosted MTAs, inspect the startup and reload configuration scripts to determine whether the process supports SIGHUP-triggered rule reloads or requires full restart on configuration change.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'reload|SIGHUP|hot.?swap|dynamic' /etc/postfix/main.cf /etc/amavis/conf.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration parameters or comments indicating reload capability; presence of reload target in init scripts or systemd unit files

option_description: Identifies the operational mechanism by which filtering rules, blocklists, and authentication policies are updated in the email gateway. Options range from fully automated feed-driven updates, to scheduled batch updates, to entirely manual administrator-initiated changes, or no update process at all.
security_impact: Required alongside live_rule_update_supported and blocklist_last_updated_days_ago in the rule_maintainability_and_updateability Rego rule. The policy accepts both automated/scheduled and manual mechanisms, but all require blocklist freshness within 7 days. Manual-only update processes introduce operational risk of stale rules during staff absence or high-pressure incident response windows, while automated mechanisms provide consistent protection against emerging threats.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Proofpoint Email Protection, navigate to Security Settings > Anti-Spam / Threat Intelligence and review the threat intelligence feed update settings, including refresh intervals and whether updates are push or pull based. In Mimecast, check Administration Console > Account > Account Settings > Anti-Spam for feed subscription status.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Proofpoint: Security Settings > Anti-Spam / Threat Intelligence | Mimecast: Administration Console > Account > Account Settings > Anti-Spam
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Feed update frequency displayed (e.g., every 15 minutes = automated); manual update button present with no schedule = manual

how_to_obtain.instruction: For on-premises mail gateways, inspect cron jobs or scheduled tasks that invoke rule update scripts to determine whether updates are automated on a schedule or absent entirely.
how_to_obtain.command: crontab -l 2>/dev/null; ls -la /etc/cron.d/ | grep -iE 'spam|mail|filter|block'; systemctl list-timers | grep -iE 'spam|mail|update'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Cron entry with recurrence schedule indicates 'scheduled'; feed daemon running continuously indicates 'automated'; no entries indicate 'manual' or 'none'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect SpamAssassin or similar open-source filter configuration for sa-update scheduled job definitions, or check ClamAV freshclam configuration for automated signature pull intervals.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/cron.d/spamassassin 2>/dev/null; cat /etc/freshclam.conf | grep -E 'Checks|DatabaseMirror|UpdateLogFile'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Checks value (e.g., Checks 24) confirms automated daily pull; cron entry confirms scheduled execution; absence of both indicates manual

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the email security administrator or review the change management runbook to confirm whether rule updates are initiated by automated feeds, a maintenance schedule, or exclusively by manual administrator action in response to incidents.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented update procedure identifying frequency and trigger mechanism; ticket history showing update cadence

option_description: Measures the number of days elapsed since the spam and threat blocklist was last successfully updated in the email gateway. Provides a freshness indicator for the currency of threat intelligence being applied to inbound and outbound mail filtering.
security_impact: Used as a threshold condition in the rule_maintainability_and_updateability Rego rule, which requires blocklist_last_updated_days_ago <= 7 regardless of whether the update mechanism is automated, scheduled, or manual. Stale blocklists allow newly identified malicious IPs, domains, and spam signatures to bypass filtering, directly reducing detection efficacy against current threat campaigns.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Log into the email gateway admin console and navigate to the threat intelligence or blocklist status section. In Proofpoint, check Security Settings > Threat Intelligence > Last Updated timestamp. In Mimecast, review Administration Console > Anti-Spam > Feed Status for the last synchronization time.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Proofpoint: Security Settings > Threat Intelligence > Feed Status | Mimecast: Administration Console > Anti-Spam > Feed Status
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Timestamp of last successful update displayed; calculate days elapsed from current date to determine attribute value

how_to_obtain.instruction: For SpamAssassin deployments, inspect the sa-update log or journal output to identify the most recent successful rule update timestamp and calculate elapsed days.
how_to_obtain.command: journalctl -u sa-update --since '30 days ago' | tail -20; grep 'update successful\|rules updated' /var/log/sa-update.log 2>/dev/null | tail -5
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log line with timestamp showing last successful update; e.g., 'update successful, 12 new rules' with date prefix

how_to_obtain.instruction: For ClamAV-integrated mail filtering, check the freshclam log or query the clamscan version output to identify the virus database creation date and calculate staleness.
how_to_obtain.command: freshclam --version 2>/dev/null; stat /var/lib/clamav/main.cvd /var/lib/clamav/daily.cvd 2>/dev/null | grep Modify; clamscan --version | grep -i database
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Modify timestamp on daily.cvd file; clamscan output showing 'ClamAV 0.x.x/XXXXX/Day Mon DD HH:MM:SS YYYY' where date indicates last update

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the email security vendor's management API for blocklist feed synchronization status. For Microsoft 365, retrieve the threat intelligence update status via the Security Graph API.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://api.mimecast.com/api/account/get-account' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -iE 'update|feed|timestamp'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response containing last update timestamp field; compute days_ago = (current_date - last_update_date).days

option_description: Controls whether the email quarantine system is actively enabled and enforcing the holding of suspect messages rather than delivering them to recipients or silently dropping them. When enabled, messages flagged by spam, malware, or policy filters are placed in a holding area pending review or automated disposition.
security_impact: Required as the primary condition in both quarantine_management_workflow Rego rules, where quarantine_enabled == true must be present alongside retention_period_days >= 7. Without an active quarantine, suspected malicious or spam messages are either delivered to end users (increasing risk of interaction with threats) or permanently deleted (preventing review of false positives and eliminating forensic opportunity).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam and inspect both inbound and outbound policies for quarantine action assignment. Confirm the quarantine action is selected for high-confidence spam and malware detections.
how_to_obtain.navigation: security.microsoft.com > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Anti-spam
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Spam detection action shows 'Move message to Quarantine' or 'Quarantine message'; quarantine policy assigned to the rule

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve the hosted content filter policy and confirm quarantine actions are assigned for spam, high-confidence spam, phishing, and malware categories.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, SpamAction, HighConfidenceSpamAction, PhishSpamAction, BulkSpamAction | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SpamAction: Quarantine; HighConfidenceSpamAction: Quarantine; PhishSpamAction: Quarantine — all confirming quarantine is enabled and active

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Postfix with amavisd-new, inspect the amavisd configuration to verify quarantine is enabled with a defined quarantine directory or SMTP quarantine relay.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'quarantine|spam_quarantine|virus_quarantine|final_spam_destiny' /etc/amavis/conf.d/*.conf /etc/amavisd.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: final_spam_destiny = D_DISCARD or D_BOUNCE with quarantine_dir defined; spam_quarantine_to set to a valid address or path

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Google Workspace with a third-party gateway, navigate to Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Compliance and verify a quarantine routing rule is active. For standalone Proofpoint, check Email Protection > Email > Quarantine Settings to confirm quarantine is active.
how_to_obtain.navigation: admin.google.com > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail > Compliance > Content compliance | Proofpoint: Email > Quarantine Settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Quarantine routing rule shown as active; quarantine settings page shows enabled status with storage backend configured

option_description: Specifies the number of days quarantined messages are retained before automatic deletion. This value determines how long administrators and end users have to review, release, or escalate held messages before they are permanently purged from the quarantine store.
security_impact: Required in both quarantine_management_workflow Rego rules, where retention_period_days >= 7 is a hard threshold. A value below 7 days reduces the window for users to recover legitimate messages held as false positives and limits forensic analysis time for confirmed threats. A value of 0 effectively disables meaningful quarantine even if the system is technically enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Quarantine Policies and review the retention setting for each active quarantine policy. The default Microsoft policy retains messages for 30 days.
how_to_obtain.navigation: security.microsoft.com > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Quarantine Policies > select policy > Retention period
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retention period field showing numeric value in days (e.g., 30 days = compliant with Rego threshold of >= 7)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve quarantine policy retention configuration for all active quarantine policies and identify any policies with retention below the 7-day threshold.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-QuarantinePolicy | Select-Object Name, QuarantineRetentionDays, EndUserQuarantinePermissionsValue | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: QuarantineRetentionDays: 30 (or another value); values below 7 indicate non-compliant configuration

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Mimecast, navigate to Administration Console > Account > Anti-Spam and locate the quarantine expiry setting. For Proofpoint, check Security Settings > Quarantine > Storage Settings for the message retention duration configuration.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Mimecast: Administration Console > Account > Anti-Spam > Quarantine expiry | Proofpoint: Security Settings > Quarantine > Storage Settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Numeric retention duration displayed in days; compare against 7-day minimum threshold requirement

how_to_obtain.instruction: For amavisd-new or SpamAssassin with file-based quarantine, inspect the quarantine directory age-out cron job or amavisd cleanup script to determine configured retention duration.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'days|mtime|quarantine.*clean|expire' /etc/cron.d/* /etc/amavis/conf.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#'; find /var/lib/amavis/quarantine -maxdepth 0 -printf 'Quarantine path exists\n' 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Find command with -mtime +N in cleanup script where N is retention days; or amavisd parameter specifying max quarantine age

option_description: Controls whether end users have access to a self-service interface (quarantine portal, digest email with release links, or user-facing web console) to review messages held in quarantine on their behalf and release false positives without administrator intervention.
security_impact: Referenced in the first quarantine_management_workflow Rego rule, which requires user_release_interface_enabled == true alongside quarantine_enabled == true, retention_period_days >= 7, and admin_review_notifications_enabled == true. Without a self-release interface, end users cannot recover false positives without submitting helpdesk tickets, increasing administrative burden and reducing user satisfaction with the email security system, which can lead to pressure to loosen filtering thresholds.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender, navigate to Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Quarantine Policies and inspect the end-user permissions for each policy. Verify that 'Allow recipients to release a message from quarantine' or 'Allow recipients to request a message to be released from quarantine' is enabled.
how_to_obtain.navigation: security.microsoft.com > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat Policies > Quarantine Policies > select policy > End-user spam notification and release settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: End-user permissions show release or request-release enabled; quarantine digest notifications configured with release link

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use Exchange Online PowerShell to retrieve quarantine policy permissions and confirm end-user quarantine access and release capabilities are enabled for the applicable policies.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-QuarantinePolicy | Select-Object Name, EndUserQuarantinePermissionsValue, EsnEnabled | Format-List
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EsnEnabled: True (quarantine digest enabled); EndUserQuarantinePermissionsValue containing release permission bit set; policies assigned to spam and bulk filter actions

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Mimecast, navigate to Administration Console > Account > Anti-Spam and verify that the user spam digest is enabled and configured to send periodic summaries with release links. For Proofpoint, check End User Services > Spam Digest to confirm digest emails are active.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Mimecast: Administration Console > Account > Anti-Spam > User spam digest | Proofpoint: End User Services > Spam Digest > Digest Settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Digest enabled with send frequency configured; release link type set to direct release or approve-to-release; target user population defined

how_to_obtain.instruction: Ask end users or review helpdesk ticket history to determine whether users receive quarantine notification emails with functional self-release links. Test the digest notification by sending a known-spam message to a test mailbox and verifying the digest arrives and the release link functions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: End users confirm receiving periodic quarantine digest emails; release links redirect to functional self-service quarantine portal; helpdesk tickets for quarantine release are low or absent

option_description: Controls whether administrators receive active notifications (email alerts, digest summaries, or push notifications) or have access to a management console dashboard with a pending-review queue for messages held in quarantine. When enabled, admins are alerted to quarantined messages so they can review potential false positives or missed detections before retention periods expire.
security_impact: In the Rego policy, admin_review_notifications_enabled == true is a required condition in both quarantine_management_workflow rule branches. Without this enabled, the quarantine_management_workflow countermeasure cannot activate, meaning quarantined messages may sit unreviewed until automatic deletion — allowing both false positives (legitimate mail lost) and missed detections (malicious mail never escalated) to go unaddressed. This is particularly critical because quarantine acts as the final safety net after spam filtering and DMARC disposition automation; human review closes the gap that automated rules cannot cover.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft 365 Defender (Exchange Online): Navigate to Microsoft 365 Defender portal > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat policies > Anti-spam policies. Open the active inbound policy, scroll to the 'Quarantine' section, and check whether 'Send end-user spam notification' and admin digest/alert settings are toggled on. For admin-specific quarantine alerts, also check Security & Compliance > Alerts > Alert policies for 'Messages have been quarantined' alert status.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft 365 Defender portal (security.microsoft.com) > Email & Collaboration > Policies & Rules > Threat policies > Anti-spam > [Active Policy] > Quarantine section; also Alerts > Alert policies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Quarantine notification toggle is set to 'On' for admins, and/or a quarantine digest alert policy exists in an enabled state.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Microsoft Exchange Online via PowerShell: Run Get-QuarantinePolicy and Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy to inspect quarantine notification settings. Check the QuarantineNotificationFrequency and ESNEnabled (End-user Spam Notification) fields. Also check alert policies with Get-ProtectionAlert filtering for quarantine-related alerts.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-ExchangeOnline; Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, QuarantineRetentionPeriod, EnableEndUserSpamNotifications, EndUserSpamNotificationFrequency; Get-QuarantinePolicy | Select-Object Name, QuarantineNotificationFrequency, MultiLanguageSetting; Get-ProtectionAlert | Where-Object {$_.Name -like '*quarantine*'} | Select-Object Name, IsEnabled, Severity
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EnableEndUserSpamNotifications = True and/or a quarantine alert policy shows IsEnabled = True with appropriate Severity level.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Microsoft Graph Security API or Exchange Online REST API to retrieve anti-spam policy details including quarantine notification configuration. This is suitable for automated compliance scanning pipelines.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -X GET 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/threatSubmission/emailThreats' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: API response includes quarantine policy objects with notification fields set to active/enabled states, or the Exchange Online PowerShell REST equivalent returns notification frequency values other than 'Never'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the email security administrator or review the incident response runbook to confirm: (1) whether quarantine digest alerts are being received by at least one admin mailbox or distribution list on a defined schedule (daily/weekly), (2) whether a dedicated quarantine review queue is monitored in the admin portal, and (3) whether there is a documented SLA for reviewing quarantined messages before the retention window expires. Request evidence such as recent quarantine notification emails or screenshots of the quarantine review dashboard with pending items.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin can produce recent quarantine digest emails or demonstrate an active quarantine review dashboard with a documented review cadence shorter than the configured retention period.

typical_values: true (recommended — required for quarantine_management_workflow countermeasure to activate)
false (default — common in organizations that have quarantine enabled but have not configured admin alerting, leaving quarantine unmonitored)
